pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: mm: per-process reclaim These day, there are many platforms available in the embedded market and they are smarter than kernel which has very limited information about working set so they want to involve memory management more heavily like android's lowmemory killer and ashmem or recent many lowmemory notifier. One of the simple imagine scenario about userspace's intelligence is that platform can manage tasks as forground and background so it would be better to reclaim background's task pages for end-user's *responsibility* although it has frequent referenced pages. This patch adds new knob "reclaim under proc/<pid>/" so task manager can reclaim any target process anytime, anywhere. It could give another method to platform for using memory efficiently. It can avoid process killing for getting free memory, which was really terrible experience because I lost my best score of game I had ever after I switch the phone call while I enjoyed the game. Reclaim file-backed pages only. echo file > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim anonymous pages only. echo anon > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim all pages echo all > /proc/PID/reclaim BUG=chromium:973963 TEST=build 4.14 for x86 Change-Id: I60a7ab5cfd4b4e065b767dd53cdd23e456e919dd Signed-off-by: Tim Murray <timmurray@google.com> Signed-off-by: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org> Signed-off-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1727258 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mm: perproc-reclaim: do not discarding file-backed pages With testing, I found sometime perproc-reclaim shows regression with more LMKD kill because LMKD still relies on the file-LRU size while perproc-reclaim could make the file-LRU smaller. This patch changes the policy of file-backed LRU shrinking. Instead of discarding pages of perprocess reclaim, just makes them easy-reclaimable pages, for instance, move active file pages to inactive, clear PG_referenced and pte access bits. With that, we could keep file-LRU bigger so that more change to hit in the cache while VM can shrink quickly when memory spike happens. vm_tools: concierge: do not keep xattrs/fflags in VM exports When exporting VMs, do not attempt to store extended attributes or "fflags" (chattr-style attributes). The files that are being archived should be normal files, aside from having the "encrypted" chattr flag set, which can't be preserved in an archive anyway. When libarchive adds files with these flags to a PAX-style tar file, it creates extra sections that GNU tar doesn't understand, which results in confusing error messages when extracting the tarball. Disable them to avoid adding the extra sections when using libarchive's "restricted pax" format so that the resulting tar file is cleanly extract-able with GNU tar and other tar implementations. cr50: use dedicated region for info1 accesses The INFO1 flash space is used for various purposes (endorsement key seed, Board ID and flags, serial number, etc.). Accessing these spaces in INFO1 is accompanied by managing the flash region registers, each time opening a window of the appropriate size, with appropriate permissions, etc, In fact none of these spaces contain a secret, to simplify things and preventing situations when concurrent accesses change the flash range window settings lets dedicate previously unused Region 7 register file to providing always open read access to INFO1. Write access will be enabled/disabled as required. In prod images write accesses will always happen from the vendor command context. In DBG images CLI commands will also have write access to INFO1. INFO1 window is accessed by other H1 based devices as well, this is why it is necessary to enable the window in the common chip code. crash-reporter: c++iza anomaly detector and have it use the journal Have anomaly_detector use the systemd journal as its log source instead of reading from /var/log/messages. Audit messages have been moved to /var/log/audit/audit.log, and attempts to make anomaly_detector read two files proved complicated: https://crrev.com/c/1630336 It was cleaner to completely rewrite anomaly detector by migrating it to C++ than to try to fit the current unit tests with the journal implementation. This has the added advantage of reducing the dependencies of the unit test and making it much faster since we no longer need to repeatedly call sleep. It's also now understood by the unit test framework as a group of multiple tests instead of one big test. Reading from journal has several advantages, most of which we aren't taking advantage of in this change, but can done in the future. Possible future improvements: * Use sd_journal_add_match and friends to make following the journal more efficient. * Save the journal cursor between boots to avoid missing certain early-boot and shutdown crashes: https://crbug.com/343954#c8 * Leverage structured audit data. Journald actually has all the audit fields we parse from the audit line as structured data. Use these instead of parsing the audit line. network_WiFi_LinkMonitorFailure: don't fail upon lack of disconnect This test is testing to ensure (a) Shill's link monitor detects a link failure (e.g., failing ARP requests) within a certain timeout and (b) the rest of the stack (driver, wpa_supplicant) responds appropriately when Shill requests a WiFi Reattach() Reattach() is just a "Reassociation attempt": https://w1.fi/wpa_supplicant/devel/dbus.html#dbus_interface which traditionally resulted in a disconnect/reconnect, but is now widened such that some drivers support the reassociation attempt directly, and therefore do not yield any disconnect. See https://crbug.com/990012#c4 for some more information about this. Anyway, the result is the 'iw event' only shows the "connected" event, with no disconnect in the meantime. This was confirmed in a WiFi sniffer packet capture. Since this behavior doesn't really violate (b), we should loosen this restriction, and avoid failing the test just because we didn't see a disconnect. A Reassociation should be as good as a Deauth/Reassociation in terms of "un-sticking" the driver. readahead: Handle readahead() calls with length larger than 32 pages The readahead() syscall isn't fully honoring the provided |count| parameter despite the man page saying "...bytes are read up to the next page boundary greater than or equal to (offset+count)". Kernels prior to v4.10 are capping the count to 32 pages (128kb). The following commit, included in versions >= 4.10, changed it to the optimal hardware I/O size which appears to be 128 pages on Eve: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/9491ae4aade6814afcfa67f4eb3e3342c2b39750 Fixing this is necessary for preloading the ARCVM system image file which after the ARCVM boot can have up to 4460 contiguous pages in core. Note that this also improves the average Chrome OS boot time as reported over 5 runs by login-prompt-visible in bootstat_summary's output by 12% on Eve. Before this change: login-prompt-visible = [ 4060, 4320, 4090, 4090, 4230 ] After this change: login-prompt-visible = [ 3420, 3770, 3700, 3690, 3690 ] BUG=b:137810150 TEST=ChromeOS boots 12% faster on Eve TEST=grep Cached /proc/meminfo doesn't grow significantly Change-Id: I41dd114a0864b509466580998d4e0dd9e21db162 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1717075 Tested-by: Philippe Liard <pliard@google.com> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org>

shill: connection: Add oif rules for all interfaces Previously, a pair of iif rules were added for all physical interfaces. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. In this case, at connect() time, the socket is still implicitly bound to INADDR_ANY (for AF_INET sockets), and source address selection must occur. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type. net-print/ippusbxd: Adding exponential backoff for print read requests Initiating read requests uses an asynchronous callback system where requests are sent to the printer and then a callback will fire with the printer's response. If the printer currently has no data to service the read request then it responds with a 0-byte message. This system lead to ippusbxd spamming the printer continuously with read requests that came back with empty responses. This change introduces exponential backoff so that if an empty response is received from the printer, ippusbxd will wait for increasingly long periods before issuing another request. This change significantly reduces syslog spam, and should result in faster communication with the printer.
